details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker with low privileges to disclose sensitive information from the server or proxy process memory to a downstream client. This occurs because certain functions responsible for writing Save Session Info Protocol Data Units (PDUs) use Stream_Seek instead of Stream_Zero for reserved padding fields, leading to the transmission of uninitialized heap memory that may contain cleartext credentials from previous sessions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. Authenticated RDP clients can exploit an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in smartcard response decoders. This occurs because the decoders fail to validate the length of Answer to Reset (ATR) fields against fixed inline arrays. By sending oversized ATR lengths, an attacker can trigger reads past memory objects, leading to process termination and a denial of service.

To mitigate this issue, disable smartcard redirection when connecting to RDP servers using FreeRDP. This can typically be achieved by using the `--disable-smartcard` command-line option for `xfreerdp` or similar configuration in other FreeRDP-based clients. Disabling smartcard redirection may impact functionality that relies on smartcard authentication or access within the RDP session.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This information disclosure vulnerability exists in the RDPGFX server's ResetGraphics Protocol Data Unit (PDU) serializer. It fails to properly initialize padding bytes, allowing a remote attacker to receive uninitialized heap memory. This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive data, including live pointers and GLib function addresses, which could defeat Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) and reveal the GLib module's base address.

Restrict network access to systems running FreeRDP server services, or disable the service if remote graphical access is not required.

1. Restrict RDP access to trusted network sources using firewalld:
# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=rdp
# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted_IP_or_CIDR>

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the server-side NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication path can result in a Denial of Service (DoS). notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is reachable only on FreeRDP server or proxy peers that configure the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback NTLM hash callback, which is reflected as Attack Complexity: High. An unauthenticated network attacker can cause a fixed 16-byte out-of-bounds heap write, so Integrity and Availability are High; Confidentiality is None. Red Hat rates this Important. Platform safeguards such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator hardening may impede reliable code execution, but they do not prevent the out-of-bounds write or process crash, so the base metrics are unchanged.

Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has rated this vulnerability as having a Moderate severity because successful exploitation requires user interaction to initiate a remote desktop session to an untrusted or compromised server, rather than targeting an exposed listening network service. While processing manipulated graphics display commands can lead to client-side memory corruption, the demonstrated impact is confined to terminating the client session via a crash. Server deployments of FreeRDP and sessions established solely with trusted remote hosts do not face exposure from arbitrary remote attackers.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the smartcard emulation feature where a smartcard context is released before its background worker thread is properly terminated. A malicious server can exploit this by sending a crafted sequence of smartcard I/O Request Packets (IRPs) to a client with smartcard redirection enabled. Successful exploitation can corrupt memory or cause the client application to crash, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via use-after-free in smartcard emulation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because an untrusted RDP server can remotely cause application crashes or heap corruption without requiring elevated privileges. The flaw affects client sessions where smartcard device redirection and emulation are actively configured, which is not engaged during standard RDP connections. In typical environments where smartcard forwarding is unused, client systems remain unaffected by this issue.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not enable smartcard redirection when establishing FreeRDP sessions.

Ensure client connection profiles and command-line invocations omit the `/smartcard` parameter (for example, launch connections using `xfreerdp /v:<server_address>` without the `/smartcard` switch). In graphical connection managers or RDP configuration files, disable smartcard forwarding. Additionally, only establish RDP sessions to trusted endpoints.

Caveats: Omitting smartcard redirection prevents the use of smartcard hardware tokens and smartcard-based authentication within the remote session.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to cancel and join the background worker thread prior to freeing the emulated SCardContext in FreeRDP smartcard emulation: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2+ (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which cancel and join the background worker thread before freeing the emulated SCardContext in Emulate_SCardReleaseContext, closing crafted sequence of smartcard IRPs containing ESTABLISHCONTEXT, long-timeout GETSTATUSCHANGE, and RELEASECONTEXT. Until patched, this is a concern on FreeRDP client sessions with smartcard redirection and smartcard emulation enabled, so Omit the /smartcard parameter from connection profiles and command-line invocations, disable smartcard forwarding in connection managers, and only establish RDP sessions to trusted endpoints. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying use-after-free defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

cwe.name: Double Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A double-free memory vulnerability in the Kerberos authentication component allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS). By sending a specially crafted Network Level Authentication (NLA) request, an attacker can corrupt server memory and cause the application process to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via crafted Kerberos authentication request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated with an Important severity rating because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger a denial of service or heap corruption across the network before establishing credentials. In Red Hat enterprise environments, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized as client-side software rather than listening services, which significantly reduces the exposed attack surface on typical installations. Exploitation specifically requires an active FreeRDP server or proxy configured with Kerberos authentication, an associated keytab, and an enabled user-to-user negotiation mechanism, limiting the likelihood of widespread exposure.
notes.title: Statement

Restrict network exposure by limiting incoming connections to trusted IP addresses or networks using `firewalld`, or disable the listening RDP service if remote desktop access is not required.

To restrict RDP access to a trusted subnet using `firewalld`:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=rdp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted_ip_or_subnet>
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Reloading firewall rules may temporarily interrupt existing network sessions and will prevent incoming RDP connections originating from outside the designated trusted subnets.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to ensure proper memory ownership or duplication of default Kerberos realm strings within the WinPR Kerberos SSPI retrieveSomeTgt routine during target principal assignment: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which duplicate or properly manage ownership of the default Kerberos realm string when assigning it to a realm-less target principal, closing crafted NLA/CredSSP u2u TGT request containing an '@' in the server-name component. Until patched, this is only a concern on FreeRDP servers or proxies configured with Kerberos authentication and user-to-user negotiation — Client-only FreeRDP installations or servers without Kerberos and u2u negotiation enabled are unaffected — so Restrict incoming network connections to the RDP listening port to trusted IP addresses using firewall rules, or disable the listening RDP service and user-to-user negotiation. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying double-free defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

cwe.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can trigger a race condition in the client by concurrently transmitting graphics reset commands alongside compressed bitmap data. This flaw leads to a use-after-free condition or out-of-bounds memory access on shared graphics decoding buffers. Consequently, an attacker can corrupt client memory, potentially causing the client application to crash resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or exposing sensitive memory contents.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Memory corruption via race condition in planar bitmap decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated as an Important severity because an untrusted endpoint can compromise client memory integrity and potentially execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the user running the session. A client system is vulnerable only when initiating a connection to an attacker-controlled remote desktop server that transmits conflicting display pipeline instructions. Although triggering this synchronization defect requires specific timing and client-initiated interaction, successful exploitation directly compromises the security boundaries of the client system.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

Restrict outbound RDP client connections to trusted, verified servers and block connections to unknown or untrusted remote desktop endpoints. As a compensating measure, Enable Address Space Layout Randomization to randomize FreeRDP process memory layout and hinder reliable code execution from heap corruption and Enable glibc safe-linking and heap metadata protection to impede heap manipulation and tcache corruption during planar buffer use-after-free exploitation. Please apply the fix when available.

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potentially execute arbitrary code on the client system. An attacker operating a malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server, or acting in a man-in-the-middle position, can exploit this issue by sending specially crafted graphics pipeline commands. This occurs due to improper surface key truncation, causing an internal table to become inconsistent and triggering a heap-based buffer overflow when data is written past allocated memory boundaries.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Heap-based buffer overflow via surface key truncation in RDPGFX
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because an untrusted or compromised remote desktop server can trigger heap memory corruption in the client process, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or application crash. To exploit this flaw, a user must actively establish a remote desktop connection to a rogue server or have their traffic intercepted by a malicious intermediary. Red Hat Enterprise Linux systems acting purely as remote desktop servers or that do not initiate outbound connections to untrusted endpoints are not exposed to this issue.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

Restrict FreeRDP client connections to verified RDP endpoints, enforce network encryption against interception, and disable the RDPGFX dynamic virtual channel in client configurations. As a compensating measure, Randomize process memory layouts with ASLR to impede reliable arbitrary code execution, Enforce full RELRO and PIE to protect the Global Offset Table from overwrites during heap corruption exploitation, Enable Control Flow Integrity to validate indirect call targets and block control-flow hijacking, Deploy EDR agents to detect anomalous post-exploitation behaviors and child processes spawned by FreeRDP, and Enforce non-executable memory protections using the NX/XD bit to block execution of shellcode in heap pages. Please apply the fix when available.t CME: CME-101 ASLR (Address Space Layout Randomization) (medium)

cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop (RD) Gateway or network attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a truncated WebSocket data frame followed by a Transport Layer Security (TLS) connection shutdown. Due to improper handling of the incomplete payload when the connection closes, the client enters an infinite loop, consuming excessive Central Processing Unit (CPU) resources until the application is terminated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via infinite loop on truncated WebSocket frame
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Moderate impact because exploitation requires a client to initiate a connection to a compromised or untrusted Remote Desktop Gateway, limiting the blast radius to client-side denial of service. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, FreeRDP is used as an interactive client utility rather than a persistent background service. An untrusted gateway responding with an incomplete transport payload before terminating the secure session causes the client process to loop indefinitely and consume processor capacity, without threatening system data confidentiality or memory integrity.
notes.title: Statement

For automated FreeRDP deployments, configure service watchdogs and automatic restarts to recover stalled processes.

cwe.name: Reachable Assertion

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted Credential Security Support Provider (CredSSP) request that omits negotiation tokens. When processing this malformed request with Network Level Authentication (NLA) enabled, the server triggers an internal assertion failure that abruptly terminates the server process and drops active client sessions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via missing negotiation tokens in CredSSP request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger an immediate server process termination without credentials or user interaction, resulting in a complete denial of service for active remote sessions. Within Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized for client-side remote desktop connectivity, and the shadow server utility is neither enabled nor executed by default. The risk is therefore confined to deployments where administrators explicitly run the shadow server with Network Level Authentication enabled and expose its listening port to untrusted networks.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

Restrict network exposure of the FreeRDP shadow server to trusted hosts or terminate the shadow server service if remote desktop sharing is not required.

1. If the shadow server is running and not needed, terminate the `freerdp-shadow-cli` process.

2. If the service must be accessible, restrict incoming connections to authorized management networks using firewalld:

firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-port=3389/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<TRUSTED_IP_OR_CIDR>
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveat: Restricting network access prevents unauthenticated remote clients from connecting to the shadow server session. Replace the port number if a non-default port was specified.

Warning: Reloading firewall rules with `firewall-cmd --reload` may temporarily disrupt active network traffic.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to isolate the FreeRDP shadow server network boundary by restricting incoming traffic to authorized management hosts or terminating freerdp-shadow-cli: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2+ (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validates CredSSP TSRequest structures to ensure missing negoTokens do not pass a null buffer to WinPrAsn1Decoder_InitMem and trigger fatal WINPR_ASSERT aborts, closing crafted CredSSP TSRequest containing only the version field and omitting negoTokens. Until patched, this is a concern on deployments running the FreeRDP shadow server with Network Level Authentication enabled and assertions active, so terminate the freerdp-shadow-cli process if desktop sharing is not required, or restrict the listening port via firewall rules strictly to trusted management IP addresses. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying reachable assertion failure defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious or compromised Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can trigger a race condition by repeatedly requesting the creation of an already active dynamic virtual channel while client data is concurrently processed. This issue leads to a use-after-free condition, allowing the server to crash the proxy process and result in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via dynamic channel race condition in proxy
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate rather than Important because successful exploitation only results in a denial of service and requires a specific, non-default proxy configuration. Under typical Red Hat enterprise deployments, the freerdp-proxy component is not configured to intercept dynamic virtual channels by default. Furthermore, triggering the condition requires routing an active client session to an untrusted or compromised backend RDP server and winning a multi-threaded timing race to terminate the proxy process.

To mitigate this issue, disable dynamic virtual channel interception in freerdp-proxy and restrict target connections to trusted hosts:

1. Operational Configuration: Ensure the proxy configuration does not specify `Intercept=drdynvc` and do not enable proxy modules that intercept dynamic virtual channels. Without dynamic channel interception enabled, the vulnerable tracker path is not invoked.
2. Network Access Controls: Restrict outbound proxy traffic exclusively to verified, trusted target RDP servers using network egress firewall rules.

Caveats: Disabling dynamic channel interception may prevent inspection or custom processing of dynamic virtual channel features. Modifying proxy configurations requires restarting the freerdp-proxy process, which will terminate active client sessions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This vulnerability allows a malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption by sending fragmented responses during Early User Authorization (EUA) authentication. Because FreeRDP fails to properly track remaining buffer space across partial network reads, incoming data advances past the allocated memory boundaries. An attacker who successfully exploits this issue triggers an out-of-bounds memory write, crashing the client application.

Successful exploitation requires user interaction to initiate a session to an untrusted or compromised endpoint capable of completing CredSSP negotiation. In Red Hat enterprise environments, FreeRDP primarily functions as an interactive client utility or backend for desktop graphical applications, which limits the blast radius strictly to the invoking user's local execution environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A compromised or malicious Remote Desktop (RD) Gateway server can send specially crafted Remote Procedure Call (RPC) network messages to a connecting client. Because the client verifies total buffer capacity instead of remaining buffer space before writing incoming data, client heap memory can be overwritten. An attacker can exploit this flaw to potentially execute arbitrary code or crash the client application, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Arbitrary code execution via RD Gateway RPC client heap buffer overflow
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because successful exploitation enables a compromised Remote Desktop Gateway to corrupt heap memory and potentially achieve arbitrary code execution with the permissions of the client user. Exploitation requires user initiation by connecting through an untrusted gateway, preventing unauthenticated remote attackers from triggering the vulnerability independently. Furthermore, standard direct RDP connections that do not route traffic through RD Gateway RPC transport are not exposed to this flaw.

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Limit FreeRDP connections strictly to trusted Remote Desktop Gateways and ensure server certificate verification is enforced.

Operational controls:
1. Avoid routing RDP connections through untrusted or unverified RD Gateways (do not supply untrusted hosts to the `/g:` or `/gw:` parameters).
2. Connect directly to target RDP servers, utilizing a trusted VPN rather than an intermediate RD Gateway where feasible.
3. Ensure strict TLS certificate validation is maintained; do not supply the `/cert:ignore` option on the command line or disable certificate validation in connection profiles.

If FreeRDP client functionality is not required on the system, remove the package:
# dnf remove freerdp

Caveats: Removing the `freerdp` package may also remove dependent desktop packages or graphical remote desktop clients (such as GNOME Connections or Remmina).

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce remaining stream buffer capacity validation rather than total capacity checks in the FreeRDP RD Gateway RPC client during fragment processing: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which verify remaining buffer capacity from the current stream offset instead of total capacity before writing incoming RPC fragments, closing all 2 injection vectors (crafted RPC BIND_ACK fragments, crafted RPC ALTER_CONTEXT_RESP fragments). Until patched, this is only a concern on FreeRDP client connections routed through an RD Gateway — Direct RDP connections not routed through RD Gateway RPC transport are unaffected — so Avoid routing RDP connections through untrusted RD Gateways, connect directly over trusted VPNs instead of intermediate gateways, and maintain strict TLS certificate validation by avoiding cert:ignore options. As a compensating measure, Enable ASLR to randomize FreeRDP memory addresses and complicate reliable exploitation following heap corruption, Enforce Full RELRO and PIE to prevent Global Offset Table overwrites and randomize code segment locations, Use Control Flow Integrity or Shadow Call Stack to validate indirect call targets against function pointer hijacking, Deploy EDR agents to monitor and detect anomalous process execution or memory injection spawned from the FreeRDP process, and Enforce NX/XD non-executable memory protections on the heap to prevent execution of injected payload code. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap-based buffer overflow defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-404 Certificate Pinning (high)

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the crypto/tls component. This vulnerability occurs during Transport Layer Security (TLS) session resumption when certificate authority (CA) settings are modified between the initial and resumed handshakes. An attacker could exploit this to bypass certificate validation, allowing a client or server to establish a connection that should have been rejected. This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a moderate flaw because it only occurs under specific conditions, such as TLS session resumption with runtime changes to certificate authority settings. Exploitation is not straightforward and requires a controlled setup. The impact is limited to certificate validation within the same component and does not affect system availability.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.

Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

cwe.name: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mime/multipart and net/textproto packages in Go. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

notes.text: A flaw was found in curl's cookie parsing logic. A malicious HTTP server can exploit this by setting 'super cookies' that bypass the Public Suffix List check. This allows an attacker-controlled origin to inject cookies that curl then transmits to unrelated third-party domains, leading to compromising request integrity.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: curl: curl: Cookie injection via malicious HTTP server using super cookies
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate: Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate (CVSS 6.5) compared to CISA's Critical (9.1). The scoring difference is due to two factors: first, exploitation requires the victim's curl to connect using a trailing-dot hostname (e.g., https://example.co.uk.), a format that is uncommon in practice and incompatible with TLS SNI; second, the direct impact is cookie injection into outbound requests — not exfiltration of victim data to the attacker. The curl project itself rates this flaw Low severity. Red Hat products that use curl for HTTP communication are affected, but the trailing-dot precondition significantly limits real-world exploitability. This flaw has not been shown to enable impacts beyond session integrity modification.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity

notes.text: A flaw was found in Eclipse Jetty. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass access controls and reach restricted resources. The issue occurs because the server and proxy components perform case-sensitive validation on host allowlists and denylists. By sending requests with altered character casing in the host name, an attacker can circumvent configured host filtering policies.

notes.text: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-server: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-proxy: Eclipse Jetty: Access control bypass via case-sensitive host filtering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw allows an attacker to bypass host-based access control in Eclipse Jetty's server and proxy components. By varying the letter case of the Host header, requests can slip past configured host allow/deny lists, letting an attacker reach resources that virtual-host or proxy filtering was meant to block in affected Red Hat products that use jetty-server or jetty-proxy for this purpose.

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

notes.text: A flaw was found in Jetty. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP/1.1 chunked requests. This can cause Jetty and an intermediary proxy to interpret different request boundaries, potentially leading to HTTP request smuggling. This issue arises from Jetty's acceptance of a lone Line Feed (LF) character as a terminator during chunked request parsing.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-http: Jetty: HTTP request smuggling via crafted chunked requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Jetty in affected Red Hat products may permit remote, unauthenticated HTTP request smuggling when specially crafted HTTP/1.1 chunked requests traverse an intermediary that interprets request boundaries differently. Jetty 12.1 uses RFC 9110 compliance by default and is not affected unless configured to use legacy RFC 7230 or RFC 2616 compliance modes. Remediation is being pursued for vulnerable shipped versions.

cwe.name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size

notes.text: A flaw was found in Bouncy Castle for Java. The DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) handshake reassembler allocates buffers based on an unchecked 24-bit length value. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted DTLS handshake message, leading to excessive memory allocation and a denial of service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.bouncycastle/bc-java: org.bouncycastle/bctls-fips: Bouncy Castle for Java: Denial of Service via unchecked DTLS handshake reassembler buffer allocation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Bouncy Castle for Java's DTLS handshake reassembler allocates a buffer from an unchecked 24-bit length field, so a remote, unauthenticated attacker who sends a specially crafted DTLS handshake message can force excessive memory allocation and cause a denial of service. Only the Bouncy Castle TLS module (bctls) contains the affected code; Red Hat products that ship only the core provider (bcprov) or other Bouncy Castle modules are not affected. Within Red Hat's portfolio, the vulnerable module is bundled by Red Hat Fuse (via Apache CXF) and Red Hat Satellite.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. A crafted CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) message can cause an 8-byte out-of-bounds heap write when it is decrypted with CMS_decrypt(). This issue occurs because the CMS decryption process incorrectly sizes the key-unwrap output buffer when using the AES-WRAP-PAD unwrap primitive. This can lead to memory corruption, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssl: heap buffer overflow in CMS key unwrapping
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker needs to supply a crafted CMS message to be decrypted in an application by CMS_decrypt(). The out-of-bounds write is a fixed-size (8-byte), fixed-value (zero) heap overflow immediately past the memory allocation, causing memory corruption, but the impact is limited to a denial of service. For these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. A crafted CMP (Certificate Management Protocol) message can cause an invalid pointer dereference due to a missing type check in the password-based protection verification. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can crash applications acting as a CMP server or client, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssl: invalid pointer dereference in CMP server via crafted protectionAlg
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs to supply a crafted CMP message to an application acting as a CMP server or client. Server applications need to be configured to accept PBM-protected messages, and client applications need to communicate with a malicious or intercepted CMP server. The missing type check causes an invalid pointer dereference, resulting in a denial of service. There is no memory disclosure, no controlled memory write and no path to code execution. For these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with a moderate severity.

This uncontrolled memory growth can lead to a denial of service (DoS) by exhausting the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) heap.

For Jackson 3.x, upgrade to 3.1.4 or later, or the first fixed release in the applicable 3.2.x stream. notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity

notes.text: A flaw was found in jackson-core. An attacker can supply specially crafted JSON that, when deserialized into a numeric target type, triggers a Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability. This occurs due to quadratic backtracking in the NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber() method's PATTERN_FLOAT regular expression. A small number of concurrent requests with a long input string can exhaust a server's request-handling thread pool, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: com.fasterxml.jackson/jackson-core: tools.jackson.core/jackson-core: Jackson-core: Denial of Service via regular expression backtracking
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because while remote actors can induce CPU starvation to trigger a denial of service, the issue affects availability only without granting unauthorized access or data tampering capabilities. In Red Hat environments, exposure depends on services deserializing untrusted JSON payloads into numeric Java object types where default string coercion occurs. Older releases packaging jackson-core versions prior to 2.17.0 do not include the vulnerable pattern matching logic and are unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop

notes.text: A flaw was found in FasterXML jackson-core. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing a specially crafted, malformed token to the JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput) method. The UTF8DataInputJsonParser component, responsible for handling DataInput sources, does not properly limit the size of the error message generated for invalid tokens. This unbounded growth of the StringBuilder can consume excessive memory, leading to an OutOfMemoryError and crashing the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: com.fasterxml.jackson.core/jackson-core: Jackson-core: Denial of Service via unbounded StringBuilder growth during malformed token processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service flaw exists in FasterXML jackson-core where processing malformed JSON tokens from a DataInput source can lead to unbounded memory allocation. This vulnerability can exhaust system resources, causing a Java Virtual Machine (JVM) crash and impacting the availability of services that utilize the affected JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput) method with untrusted input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mime/multipart and net/textproto packages in Go. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted sequence of progressive display tile updates to a connecting client. Because decompression buffers are allocated without being initialized, processing these updates can trigger an internal assertion failure that terminates the client application or causes uninitialized heap memory to be rendered directly onto the screen. This allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or disclose sensitive information.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via uninitialized progressive tile handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important rather than Moderate because a compromised or malicious remote desktop endpoint can trigger an unhandled crash or leak uninitialized process memory to the client display without requiring privileges. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized to establish outbound remote desktop sessions, meaning exposure depends on connecting to an untrusted server. While the attack occurs over the network, exploitation relies on user interaction to initiate the connection to a rogue host rather than exposing a continuously listening network service.

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted MP3 audio data to a connected client. Due to an incorrect buffer size calculation during audio decoding, decoded audio data can be written beyond allocated memory limits, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This flaw allows an attacker to crash the client application, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap-based buffer overflow during MP3 audio decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated Important because crafted MP3 audio from a malicious RDP server can cause a heap buffer overflow in the client after the user connects (UI:R), with integrity and availability impact and limited confidentiality impact (CVSS 7.1). Decode-path constraints keep Attack Complexity High. Allocator hardening may impede exploitation but does not clear I:H/A:H.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the server-side NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication path can result in a Denial of Service (DoS). When processing authentication messages with hash callbacks enabled, FreeRDP fails to properly validate the Message Integrity Check (MIC) offset. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted authentication message, corrupting heap memory and causing the server to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap out-of-bounds write in NTLM authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is reachable only on FreeRDP server or proxy peers that configure the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback NTLM hash callback, which is reflected as Attack Complexity: High. An unauthenticated network attacker can cause a fixed 16-byte out-of-bounds heap write, so Integrity and Availability are High; Confidentiality is None. Red Hat rates this Important. Platform safeguards such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator hardening may impede reliable code execution, but they do not prevent the out-of-bounds write or process crash, so the base metrics are unchanged.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not expose FreeRDP server or proxy endpoints that use SspiNtlmHashCallback to untrusted networks; restrict access with a host firewall and network segmentation. If the NTLM hash callback is not required, leave it unset so the vulnerable MIC path is not entered.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds validation on Message Integrity Check (MIC) offsets within the authenticate message buffer before writing in ntlm_computeMicValue: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.0 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validate that the MIC offset is within the authenticate message buffer bounds before writing bytes, closing crafted NTLM AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with backward session-key offset and out-of-bounds MIC offset. Until patched, this is a concern on FreeRDP server and proxy instances configured with the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback setting, so leave SspiNtlmHashCallback unset if NTLM hash callbacks are not required, and restrict network access to FreeRDP endpoints from untrusted networks using firewalls and network segmentation. As a compensating measure, configure systemd service restart and watchdog settings to automatically restart FreeRDP upon process crashes and mitigate prolonged denial of service, require pre-authentication through a zero-trust gateway or identity-aware proxy before clients can reach the FreeRDP NTLM authentication handler, and restrict FreeRDP port access with host firewalls using firewalld or nftables to isolate the service from untrusted networks. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap out-of-bounds write defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)
