notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

go list -m golang.org/x/net
govulncheck ./...

notes.text: A flaw was found in crypto/tls. A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash server processes without requiring privileges or user interaction. Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mime/multipart and net/textproto packages in Go. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. An unauthenticated attacker can repeatedly access the OAuth login route with unique values. This can lead to unbounded memory growth, eventually exhausting system memory and causing the Grafana instance to crash. This results in a denial of service for legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The flaw in Grafana is rated Moderate, as an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a denial of service by repeatedly accessing the OAuth login route, leading to unbounded memory growth and instance crashes.

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to the Grafana instance to trusted internal networks or localhost. If a reverse proxy or load balancer is deployed in front of Grafana, configure it to implement rate limiting on requests to the OAuth login endpoint to prevent an attacker from exhausting system resources. If OAuth is not required, consider disabling it in the Grafana configuration, though this may impact user authentication workflows.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. When extracting plugin archives, Grafana did not safely resolve symbolic links. A remote attacker could craft a malicious plugin archive with symbolic links to escape the plugin installation directory. This allows the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute malicious code with the privileges of the Grafana server process, leading to remote code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: PLUGIN ARCHIVE EXTRACTION ESCAPES THE PLUGIN DIRECTORY, ALLOWING CODE EXECUTION
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Grafana's plugin extraction process is vulnerable to symbolic link traversal, enabling an attacker to write arbitrary files and achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the Grafana server. This critical flaw allows malicious code execution even before plugin signature verification, posing a significant risk in Red Hat deployments where Grafana is used.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

While no configuration fully mitigates this issue, exposure can be reduced by limiting plugin installations to vetted and pinned sets of plugins from trusted sources. Additionally, disable the `plugin_admin_enabled` setting in the Grafana configuration if not required, to prevent non-administrator users from installing plugins. This can be done by setting `plugin_admin_enabled = false` in the `[plugins]` section of the `grafana.ini` configuration file. A restart of the Grafana service may be required for changes to take effect, which could temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw in Grafana's Auth Proxy IPv6 allow-list incorrectly defaults to a broad /32 subnet mask instead of a strict /128. This misconfiguration allows remote attackers to bypass access restrictions, potentially leading to unauthorized access and data manipulation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: Grafana Auth Proxy: Unauthorized access due to incorrect IPv6 allow-list default
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw in Grafana's Auth Proxy IPv6 allow-list defaults to an overly broad /32 mask, potentially allowing unauthorized access. This strictly affects Auth Proxy deployments using IPv6 allow-lists; other authentication methods are unaffected. This has been rated moderate since auth proxy authentication is not enabled by default on grafana shipped on RHEL.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this issue, explicitly specify the intended IPv6 address mask—typically /128 for a single host—within the Grafana Auth Proxy allow-list configuration. This overrides the incorrect default /32 mask, ensuring that network access restrictions are applied strictly as intended.
For RHEL: Update the whitelist directive under the [auth.proxy] section in /etc/grafana/grafana.ini. For example, if ::1 is the desired address, configure it explicitly as ::1/128. A restart of the Grafana service (systemctl restart grafana-server) is required for the changes to take effect.

This grants the editor administrative control over the targeted dashboard, potentially leading to unauthorized data manipulation or exposure within the Grafana environment.

Red Hat's default deployment does not grant edit access to normal users. Hence, this is rated moderate.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.

Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text:
An update for delve is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Delve is a debugger for the Go programming language. The goal of the project is to provide a simple, full featured debugging tool for Go. Delve should be easy to invoke and easy to use. Chances are if you're using a debugger, things aren't going your way. With that in mind, Delve should stay out of your way as much as possible.

Security Fix(es):

* net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers (CVE-2026-78667)

* crypto/tls: golang: crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple ECH outer extension references (CVE-2026-97031)

* net/textproto: mime/multipart: golang: golang: Denial of Service via memory limit bypass in multipart form parsing (CVE-2026-94440)

* net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames (CVE-2026-78669)

* crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. This can be achieved by setting the `GODEBUG` environment variable to `netdns=go`. For example, to run a Go application with this mitigation: `GODEBUG=netdns=go /path/to/your/go/application`. This change may require restarting affected applications or services to take effect. Users should verify that this change does not negatively impact DNS resolution for their specific application environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

* freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via grayscale JPEG clipboard conversion (CVE-2026-110839)

* freerdp: freerdp: Arbitrary code execution via crafted persistent cache file (CVE-2026-111381)

* freerdp: FreeRDP: heap buffer overflow in server rdpsnd via crafted audio formats (CVE-2026-114045)

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted sequence of progressive display tile updates to a connecting client. Because decompression buffers are allocated without being initialized, processing these updates can trigger an internal assertion failure that terminates the client application or causes uninitialized heap memory to be rendered directly onto the screen. This allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or disclose sensitive information.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via uninitialized progressive tile handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important rather than Moderate because a compromised or malicious remote desktop endpoint can trigger an unhandled crash or leak uninitialized process memory to the client display without requiring privileges. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized to establish outbound remote desktop sessions, meaning exposure depends on connecting to an untrusted server. While the attack occurs over the network, exploitation relies on user interaction to initiate the connection to a rogue host rather than exposing a continuously listening network service.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. When a user connects to a malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server, the server can trigger an invalid smartcard connect operation, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability where previously released memory is accessed. A remote attacker can exploit this issue to cause memory corruption, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) through an application crash.

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP 3.0.0-beta1 before 3.32.0 Use-After-Free via Smartcard Connect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated Important because a malicious RDP peer can trigger memory corruption in the FreeRDP client after the user connects (UI:R), with potential impact beyond a simple crash. Red Hat heap/allocator hardening and ASLR raise exploitation difficulty but do not justify lowering Confidentiality/Integrity/Availability in the base score when corruption is confirmed. This is the highest-severity issue in this FreeRDP set (CVSS 8.8) but remains Important rather than Critical because exploitation requires the user to connect to a malicious RDP server (UI:R).

cwe.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending repeated serial device creation requests when serial port redirection is enabled. Because FreeRDP fails to release previous communication handles before allocating new ones, the client application exhausts available file descriptors and terminates unexpectedly.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via file descriptor exhaustion in serial device handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate for Red Hat Enterprise Linux because the impact is confined to client-side denial of service and requires an explicit, non-default feature configuration. FreeRDP does not enable serial device redirection by default, meaning an attacker-controlled RDP server can only trigger descriptor exhaustion if the client session specifically opted into serial forwarding. Additionally, the flaw affects only availability without impacting system confidentiality or data integrity.

cwe.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. The proxy component fails to enforce cumulative or absolute size limits when reassembling Remote Desktop Protocol Device Redirection (RDPDR) channel fragments. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting an initial fragment followed by continuous data fragments without a termination marker, causing unbounded memory retention in the proxy session. This excessive memory consumption can ultimately lead to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via unbounded memory consumption during RDPDR reassembly
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity because exploitation requires an established session with device redirection and a proxy explicitly configured to intercept RDPDR channel traffic, resulting in resource exhaustion without compromising data integrity, confidentiality, or allowing arbitrary code execution. In standard Red Hat deployments, FreeRDP is predominantly utilized as a client application or library rather than an intermediary proxy service. Consequently, typical environments are not exposed to this issue unless the proxy is actively deployed with channel interception enabled. Furthermore, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9 are unaffected because they provide earlier FreeRDP versions lacking the vulnerable proxy code.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server memory. When processing Network Level Authentication (NLA) connections over Transport Layer Security (TLS), the server misinterprets invalid protocol bytes as an incomplete packet rather than rejecting them. This triggers unbounded receive buffer growth as incoming data is streamed, consuming server memory until the service becomes unresponsive or crashes.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has rated this vulnerability as having an Important impact because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server memory prior to authentication without requiring valid user credentials or privileges. While FreeRDP packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux are primarily utilized for client-side connectivity, server implementations and services utilizing FreeRDP server libraries with Network Level Authentication are exposed to denial of service from unbounded buffer growth. Deployments that solely execute FreeRDP as an outbound client remain unaffected.

Restrict network access to systems running FreeRDP server services, or disable the service if remote graphical access is not required.

1. Restrict RDP access to trusted network sources using firewalld:
# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=rdp
# firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted_IP_or_CIDR>
# firewall-cmd --reload

2. If remote desktop access is not required, disable the remote desktop service (for example, GNOME Remote Desktop):
# systemctl --user --now mask gnome-remote-desktop.service

Caveats and Warnings:
Reloading firewall configurations applies changes immediately and will drop traffic from unlisted networks, which can disrupt active sessions. Stopping or masking remote desktop services immediately terminates existing user sessions and disables incoming remote desktop connectivity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted persistent cache file. When processing the malformed cache file, an arithmetic calculation error causes an undersized memory buffer to be allocated, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow during data read operations.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Arbitrary code execution via crafted persistent cache file
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An important-severity heap-based buffer overflow was found in FreeRDP's persistent bitmap cache handling. When FreeRDP loads a persistent cache file, an integer wraparound in the size calculation in persist_cache_get_data, triggered by large attacker-controlled width and height values in a crafted v3 persistent cache file, causes an undersized buffer to be allocated, which is then overflowed when the entry is read in persistent_cache_read_entry_v3. A local attacker who can place a crafted persistent cache file and have it loaded by a user could use this flaw to crash the FreeRDP client or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the client process. The freerdp component is affected as shipped in multiple Red Hat Enterprise Linux versions, in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and in the Fedora and EPEL community streams, where a fix is being pursued; the Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 Extended Lifecycle Support stream is out of support scope. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.3, consistent with the upstream severity assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This flaw allows arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) when parsing persistent cache files. A local attacker can trigger this vulnerability by tricking a user into loading a maliciously crafted cache file containing oversized image dimensions. This manipulation leads to an integer calculation error and a heap-based buffer overflow, causing memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Arbitrary code execution via crafted persistent cache file
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in FreeRDP's persistent cache v2 parser (persistent_cache_read_entry_v2 in libfreerdp/cache/persistent.c). An integer wraparound in the bitmap size calculation allows a crafted persistent cache v2 file containing oversized width and height values to bypass bounds checks, causing mismatched entry size accounting and fixed 16 KiB reads that corrupt heap memory. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by convincing a user to load a maliciously crafted persistent cache file, resulting in a crash of the FreeRDP client or potential arbitrary code execution in the context of the user running the client. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT (CVSS 7.3, CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream Important rating, with exploitation requiring user interaction to load the attacker-supplied cache file. The freerdp package as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, 8, 9, and 10, freerdp and freerdp2 in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and freerdp and freerdp2 in Fedora and EPEL are affected, and fixes for these products are being pursued.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the server-side NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication path can result in a Denial of Service (DoS). When processing authentication messages with hash callbacks enabled, FreeRDP fails to properly validate the Message Integrity Check (MIC) offset. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted authentication message, corrupting heap memory and causing the server to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap out-of-bounds write in NTLM authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is reachable only on FreeRDP server or proxy peers that configure the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback NTLM hash callback, which is reflected as Attack Complexity: High. An unauthenticated network attacker can cause a fixed 16-byte out-of-bounds heap write, so Integrity and Availability are High; Confidentiality is None. Red Hat rates this Important. Platform safeguards such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator hardening may impede reliable code execution, but they do not prevent the out-of-bounds write or process crash, so the base metrics are unchanged.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not expose FreeRDP server or proxy endpoints that use SspiNtlmHashCallback to untrusted networks; restrict access with a host firewall and network segmentation. If the NTLM hash callback is not required, leave it unset so the vulnerable MIC path is not entered.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds validation on Message Integrity Check (MIC) offsets within the authenticate message buffer before writing in ntlm_computeMicValue: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.0 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validate that the MIC offset is within the authenticate message buffer bounds before writing bytes, closing crafted NTLM AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with backward session-key offset and out-of-bounds MIC offset. Until patched, this is a concern on FreeRDP server and proxy instances configured with the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback setting, so leave SspiNtlmHashCallback unset if NTLM hash callbacks are not required, and restrict network access to FreeRDP endpoints from untrusted networks using firewalls and network segmentation. As a compensating measure, configure systemd service restart and watchdog settings to automatically restart FreeRDP upon process crashes and mitigate prolonged denial of service, require pre-authentication through a zero-trust gateway or identity-aware proxy before clients can reach the FreeRDP NTLM authentication handler, and restrict FreeRDP port access with host firewalls using firewalld or nftables to isolate the service from untrusted networks. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap out-of-bounds write defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

When launching sessions with the xfreerdp command-line utility, explicitly disable the clipboard channel:

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can cause a denial of service (DoS) or memory corruption on a connecting client. This issue occurs because FreeRDP does not properly validate graphical surface dimensions, resulting in an integer overflow during memory allocation calculations. By sending a specially crafted surface creation message, a rogue server can trigger excessive memory consumption or a heap-based buffer overflow, causing the client application to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Heap buffer overflow via integer overflow in surface creation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as Moderate impact for Red Hat products because exploitation requires client-side user interaction to connect to an untrusted remote system, restricting the potential blast radius to the local application session. On standard 64-bit Red Hat Enterprise Linux architectures, the arithmetic wrap does not occur; instead, the oversized dimension request triggers an excessively large memory allocation that terminates the client process rather than corrupting memory. As a result, an attacker is limited to causing a denial of service on the client without compromising host system integrity or achieving arbitrary code execution.

Restrict exposure by limiting RDP network traffic to trusted hosts or subnets using firewalld:

1. Add the trusted administrative subnet to the trusted zone:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted_ip_or_subnet>

2. Remove general access to the RDP port (default 3389/tcp) from public zones:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-port=3389/tcp

3. Apply the firewall configuration:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Reloading firewall rules may briefly interrupt active network sessions.

Additionally, stop any running `freerdp-shadow-cli` or custom FreeRDP server processes if remote session sharing is not actively required.

Caveat: Network access controls mitigate untrusted exposure but do not defend against malicious input sent by authorized clients within the permitted network.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in freerdp-proxy when processing Bitmap Cache v2 capability sets. The proxy accepts a client-declared numCellCaches value below five and later indexes the bitmap cache cell array at fixed positions 0 through 4. A client that connects to the proxy and completes capability exchange can cause heap corruption, disclosure of adjacent heap contents to the backend server, or a crash of the proxy process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Out-of-bounds write in proxy bitmap cache v2 capability handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important rather than Critical. A remote client can trigger memory corruption in freerdp-proxy without additional user interaction on the proxy host, but freerdp-proxy is not enabled or exposed by default and must be deliberately deployed. Turning the constrained out-of-bounds write into reliable arbitrary code execution depends on heap layout and a fully established proxy path to a backend server. Confirmed impacts include proxy process crash and potential heap content leakage to the backend. This Important rating aligns with the upstream High severity advisory rather than a Critical network-service compromise on a default Red Hat deployment.

cwe.name: Use After Free

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the client's Remote Desktop Protocol Graphics (RDPGFX) dynamic virtual channel handling. A malicious RDP server can open a second dynamic virtual channel that reuses an already registered channel name with a different ChannelId, overwriting the listener's single callback slot. When that second channel is closed, the callback is freed without clearing the slot. A subsequent PDU on the original channel then dereferences freed memory, which can crash the client or potentially lead to arbitrary code execution.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

Once connected with the graphics pipeline enabled, a hostile server can trigger a use-after-free in the FreeRDP client process that may allow code execution with the privileges of the client user. Standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux hardening such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator protections may impede reliable code execution but does not remove the denial-of-service impact from a client crash.

The highest-value action is to isolate the FreeRDP shadow server network boundary by restricting incoming traffic to authorized management hosts or terminating freerdp-shadow-cli: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2+ (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validates CredSSP TSRequest structures to ensure missing negoTokens do not pass a null buffer to WinPrAsn1Decoder_InitMem and trigger fatal WINPR_ASSERT aborts, closing crafted CredSSP TSRequest containing only the version field and omitting negoTokens. Until patched, this is a concern on deployments running the FreeRDP shadow server with Network Level Authentication enabled and assertions active, so terminate the freerdp-shadow-cli process if desktop sharing is not required, or restrict the listening port via firewall rules strictly to trusted management IP addresses. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying reachable assertion failure defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious or compromised Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can trigger a race condition by repeatedly requesting the creation of an already active dynamic virtual channel while client data is concurrently processed. This issue leads to a use-after-free condition, allowing the server to crash the proxy process and result in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via dynamic channel race condition in proxy
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Moderate rather than Important because successful exploitation only results in a denial of service and requires a specific, non-default proxy configuration. Under typical Red Hat enterprise deployments, the freerdp-proxy component is not configured to intercept dynamic virtual channels by default. Furthermore, triggering the condition requires routing an active client session to an untrusted or compromised backend RDP server and winning a multi-threaded timing race to terminate the proxy process.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this issue, disable dynamic virtual channel interception in freerdp-proxy and restrict target connections to trusted hosts:

1. Operational Configuration: Ensure the proxy configuration does not specify `Intercept=drdynvc` and do not enable proxy modules that intercept dynamic virtual channels. Without dynamic channel interception enabled, the vulnerable tracker path is not invoked.
2. Network Access Controls: Restrict outbound proxy traffic exclusively to verified, trusted target RDP servers using network egress firewall rules.

Caveats: Disabling dynamic channel interception may prevent inspection or custom processing of dynamic virtual channel features. Modifying proxy configurations requires restarting the freerdp-proxy process, which will terminate active client sessions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. This vulnerability allows a malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption by sending fragmented responses during Early User Authorization (EUA) authentication. Because FreeRDP fails to properly track remaining buffer space across partial network reads, incoming data advances past the allocated memory boundaries. An attacker who successfully exploits this issue triggers an out-of-bounds memory write, crashing the client application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap buffer overflow during Early User Authorization
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an attacker-controlled remote desktop server can trigger heap memory corruption or terminate the client process upon connection, presenting a high risk to client integrity and availability rather than a lower-severity transient failure. Successful exploitation requires user interaction to initiate a session to an untrusted or compromised endpoint capable of completing CredSSP negotiation. In Red Hat enterprise environments, FreeRDP primarily functions as an interactive client utility or backend for desktop graphical applications, which limits the blast radius strictly to the invoking user's local execution environment.

By sending audio data packets over a dynamic virtual channel and immediately closing the connection, the server triggers a use-after-free condition where the client's audio playback thread accesses already released memory.

In typical enterprise environments, RDP sessions are established with known, managed systems, substantially limiting exposure to rogue servers. Furthermore, the flaw only impacts client sessions handling audio redirection over dynamic channels, and the blast radius is confined to the individual client process.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A compromised or malicious Remote Desktop (RD) Gateway server can send specially crafted Remote Procedure Call (RPC) network messages to a connecting client. Because the client verifies total buffer capacity instead of remaining buffer space before writing incoming data, client heap memory can be overwritten. An attacker can exploit this flaw to potentially execute arbitrary code or crash the client application, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Arbitrary code execution via RD Gateway RPC client heap buffer overflow
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because successful exploitation enables a compromised Remote Desktop Gateway to corrupt heap memory and potentially achieve arbitrary code execution with the permissions of the client user. Exploitation requires user initiation by connecting through an untrusted gateway, preventing unauthenticated remote attackers from triggering the vulnerability independently. Furthermore, standard direct RDP connections that do not route traffic through RD Gateway RPC transport are not exposed to this flaw.
notes.title: Statement

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Limit FreeRDP connections strictly to trusted Remote Desktop Gateways and ensure server certificate verification is enforced.

Operational controls:
1. Avoid routing RDP connections through untrusted or unverified RD Gateways (do not supply untrusted hosts to the `/g:` or `/gw:` parameters).
2. Connect directly to target RDP servers, utilizing a trusted VPN rather than an intermediate RD Gateway where feasible.
3. Ensure strict TLS certificate validation is maintained; do not supply the `/cert:ignore` option on the command line or disable certificate validation in connection profiles.

If FreeRDP client functionality is not required on the system, remove the package:
# dnf remove freerdp

Caveats: Removing the `freerdp` package may also remove dependent desktop packages or graphical remote desktop clients (such as GNOME Connections or Remmina).

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce remaining stream buffer capacity validation rather than total capacity checks in the FreeRDP RD Gateway RPC client during fragment processing: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.2 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which verify remaining buffer capacity from the current stream offset instead of total capacity before writing incoming RPC fragments, closing all 2 injection vectors (crafted RPC BIND_ACK fragments, crafted RPC ALTER_CONTEXT_RESP fragments). Until patched, this is only a concern on FreeRDP client connections routed through an RD Gateway — Direct RDP connections not routed through RD Gateway RPC transport are unaffected — so Avoid routing RDP connections through untrusted RD Gateways, connect directly over trusted VPNs instead of intermediate gateways, and maintain strict TLS certificate validation by avoiding cert:ignore options. As a compensating measure, Enable ASLR to randomize FreeRDP memory addresses and complicate reliable exploitation following heap corruption, Enforce Full RELRO and PIE to prevent Global Offset Table overwrites and randomize code segment locations, Use Control Flow Integrity or Shadow Call Stack to validate indirect call targets against function pointer hijacking, Deploy EDR agents to monitor and detect anomalous process execution or memory injection spawned from the FreeRDP process, and Enforce NX/XD non-executable memory protections on the heap to prevent execution of injected payload code. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap-based buffer overflow defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-404 Certificate Pinning (high)

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted sequence of progressive display tile updates to a connecting client. Because decompression buffers are allocated without being initialized, processing these updates can trigger an internal assertion failure that terminates the client application or causes uninitialized heap memory to be rendered directly onto the screen. This allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or disclose sensitive information.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important rather than Moderate because a compromised or malicious remote desktop endpoint can trigger an unhandled crash or leak uninitialized process memory to the client display without requiring privileges. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized to establish outbound remote desktop sessions, meaning exposure depends on connecting to an untrusted server. While the attack occurs over the network, exploitation relies on user interaction to initiate the connection to a rogue host rather than exposing a continuously listening network service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted MP3 audio data to a connected client. Due to an incorrect buffer size calculation during audio decoding, decoded audio data can be written beyond allocated memory limits, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This flaw allows an attacker to crash the client application, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: This flaw is rated Important because crafted MP3 audio from a malicious RDP server can cause a heap buffer overflow in the client after the user connects (UI:R), with integrity and availability impact and limited confidentiality impact (CVSS 7.1). Decode-path constraints keep Attack Complexity High. Allocator hardening may impede exploitation but does not clear I:H/A:H.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the server-side NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication path can result in a Denial of Service (DoS). When processing authentication messages with hash callbacks enabled, FreeRDP fails to properly validate the Message Integrity Check (MIC) offset. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted authentication message, corrupting heap memory and causing the server to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap out-of-bounds write in NTLM authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is reachable only on FreeRDP server or proxy peers that configure the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback NTLM hash callback, which is reflected as Attack Complexity: High. An unauthenticated network attacker can cause a fixed 16-byte out-of-bounds heap write, so Integrity and Availability are High; Confidentiality is None. Red Hat rates this Important. Platform safeguards such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator hardening may impede reliable code execution, but they do not prevent the out-of-bounds write or process crash, so the base metrics are unchanged.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not expose FreeRDP server or proxy endpoints that use SspiNtlmHashCallback to untrusted networks; restrict access with a host firewall and network segmentation. If the NTLM hash callback is not required, leave it unset so the vulnerable MIC path is not entered.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds validation on Message Integrity Check (MIC) offsets within the authenticate message buffer before writing in ntlm_computeMicValue: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.0 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validate that the MIC offset is within the authenticate message buffer bounds before writing bytes, closing crafted NTLM AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with backward session-key offset and out-of-bounds MIC offset. Until patched, this is a concern on FreeRDP server and proxy instances configured with the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback setting, so leave SspiNtlmHashCallback unset if NTLM hash callbacks are not required, and restrict network access to FreeRDP endpoints from untrusted networks using firewalls and network segmentation. As a compensating measure, configure systemd service restart and watchdog settings to automatically restart FreeRDP upon process crashes and mitigate prolonged denial of service, require pre-authentication through a zero-trust gateway or identity-aware proxy before clients can reach the FreeRDP NTLM authentication handler, and restrict FreeRDP port access with host firewalls using firewalld or nftables to isolate the service from untrusted networks. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap out-of-bounds write defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

A remote attacker can trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet containing multiple Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) outer extension references to a server. Processing these unauthorized references leads to excessive memory consumption, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) through server crashes or unresponsiveness.

Go applications that terminate TLS connections and accept Encrypted Client Hello configurations are vulnerable to resource amplification during the initial handshake. While the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data confidentiality, the resulting denial of service can disrupt critical network services.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted sequence of progressive display tile updates to a connecting client. Because decompression buffers are allocated without being initialized, processing these updates can trigger an internal assertion failure that terminates the client application or causes uninitialized heap memory to be rendered directly onto the screen. This allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or disclose sensitive information.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: FreeRDP: Denial of Service via uninitialized progressive tile handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important rather than Moderate because a compromised or malicious remote desktop endpoint can trigger an unhandled crash or leak uninitialized process memory to the client display without requiring privileges. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux, FreeRDP packages are primarily utilized to establish outbound remote desktop sessions, meaning exposure depends on connecting to an untrusted server. While the attack occurs over the network, exploitation relies on user interaction to initiate the connection to a rogue host rather than exposing a continuously listening network service.

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. A malicious Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) server can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted MP3 audio data to a connected client. Due to an incorrect buffer size calculation during audio decoding, decoded audio data can be written beyond allocated memory limits, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This flaw allows an attacker to crash the client application, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap-based buffer overflow during MP3 audio decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated Important because crafted MP3 audio from a malicious RDP server can cause a heap buffer overflow in the client after the user connects (UI:R), with integrity and availability impact and limited confidentiality impact (CVSS 7.1). Decode-path constraints keep Attack Complexity High. Allocator hardening may impede exploitation but does not clear I:H/A:H.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
