cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in FreeRDP. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the server-side NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication path can result in a Denial of Service (DoS). When processing authentication messages with hash callbacks enabled, FreeRDP fails to properly validate the Message Integrity Check (MIC) offset. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted authentication message, corrupting heap memory and causing the server to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: freerdp: freerdp: Denial of Service via heap out-of-bounds write in NTLM authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is reachable only on FreeRDP server or proxy peers that configure the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback NTLM hash callback, which is reflected as Attack Complexity: High. An unauthenticated network attacker can cause a fixed 16-byte out-of-bounds heap write, so Integrity and Availability are High; Confidentiality is None. Red Hat rates this Important. Platform safeguards such as ASLR, NX, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and glibc allocator hardening may impede reliable code execution, but they do not prevent the out-of-bounds write or process crash, so the base metrics are unchanged.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Do not expose FreeRDP server or proxy endpoints that use SspiNtlmHashCallback to untrusted networks; restrict access with a host firewall and network segmentation. If the NTLM hash callback is not required, leave it unset so the vulnerable MIC path is not entered.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds validation on Message Integrity Check (MIC) offsets within the authenticate message buffer before writing in ntlm_computeMicValue: upgrade to FreeRDP 3.32.0 (or the fixed Freerdp builds), which validate that the MIC offset is within the authenticate message buffer bounds before writing bytes, closing crafted NTLM AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with backward session-key offset and out-of-bounds MIC offset. Until patched, this is a concern on FreeRDP server and proxy instances configured with the non-default SspiNtlmHashCallback setting, so leave SspiNtlmHashCallback unset if NTLM hash callbacks are not required, and restrict network access to FreeRDP endpoints from untrusted networks using firewalls and network segmentation. As a compensating measure, configure systemd service restart and watchdog settings to automatically restart FreeRDP upon process crashes and mitigate prolonged denial of service, require pre-authentication through a zero-trust gateway or identity-aware proxy before clients can reach the FreeRDP NTLM authentication handler, and restrict FreeRDP port access with host firewalls using firewalld or nftables to isolate the service from untrusted networks. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying heap out-of-bounds write defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

notes.text: A flaw was found in Django. GeoDjango's spatial lookups can be exploited by a staff user with view permissions who submits a specially crafted spatial-field filter. This vulnerability allows an attacker to write arbitrary files to the server, which can lead to remote code execution. Additionally, it can be used to make outbound network requests, resulting in server-side request forgery.

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity

notes.text: A flaw was found in Eclipse Jetty. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass access controls and reach restricted resources. The issue occurs because the server and proxy components perform case-sensitive validation on host allowlists and denylists. By sending requests with altered character casing in the host name, an attacker can circumvent configured host filtering policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-server: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-proxy: Eclipse Jetty: Access control bypass via case-sensitive host filtering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw allows an attacker to bypass host-based access control in Eclipse Jetty's server and proxy components. By varying the letter case of the Host header, requests can slip past configured host allow/deny lists, letting an attacker reach resources that virtual-host or proxy filtering was meant to block in affected Red Hat products that use jetty-server or jetty-proxy for this purpose.
notes.title: Statement

There is no mitigation for this issue other than applying the fix. As a temporary workaround, administrators who rely on Jetty host allow/deny filtering should add case-variant duplicates of every configured hostname to the filter lists, or enforce hostname case-normalization at an upstream load balancer or reverse proxy, until the update is installed.

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

notes.text: A flaw was found in Jetty. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP/1.1 chunked requests. This can cause Jetty and an intermediary proxy to interpret different request boundaries, potentially leading to HTTP request smuggling. This issue arises from Jetty's acceptance of a lone Line Feed (LF) character as a terminator during chunked request parsing.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: org.eclipse.jetty/jetty-http: Jetty: HTTP request smuggling via crafted chunked requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Jetty in affected Red Hat products may permit remote, unauthenticated HTTP request smuggling when specially crafted HTTP/1.1 chunked requests traverse an intermediary that interprets request boundaries differently. Jetty 12.1 uses RFC 9110 compliance by default and is not affected unless configured to use legacy RFC 7230 or RFC 2616 compliance modes. Remediation is being pursued for vulnerable shipped versions.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to create arbitrary Git directories outside the intended clone destination. By manipulating the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning, an attacker can redirect repository metadata to an attacker-controlled filesystem path. This could lead to arbitrary directory creation and potentially enable the execution of malicious code through Git hooks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Arbitrary Code Execution via Path Traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has identified a path traversal vulnerability in GitPython versions before 3.1.59. The vulnerability arises because the `--separate-git-dir` option is not included in the `unsafe_git_clone_options` denylist, allowing attackers who control the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning to redirect Git repository metadata to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended clone destination. This can lead to arbitrary directory and file creation bounded only by process permissions. When combined with subsequent Git operations that trigger hook execution on the redirected repository, this vulnerability can escalate to arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that the application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the `separate_git_dir` keyword argument of `Repo.clone_from()` or `Repo.clone()` methods without proper validation, while the `allow_unsafe_options` parameter remains at its default value of False.

cwe.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. A remote attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing a malicious repository containing commit or tag objects with long, space-filled lines lacking a valid timestamp or timezone. When parsing these lines, the regular expression pattern triggers quadratic backtracking, leading to high CPU consumption and causing the application to become unresponsive.

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Denial of Service via regular expression backtracking in date parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because Red Hat services and containerized environments that ingest remote repositories can be exposed to sustained service outages without requiring administrative privileges or local system access. When an integration processes a repository that includes specifically structured author or tag metadata, the regex evaluation experiences severe resource exhaustion, stalling worker processes. While this defect disrupts service availability across automation workflows and analysis pipelines, it does not allow unauthorized data access or arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. A remote attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying specially crafted repository URLs that are processed without proper protocol validation. Because the library forwards untrusted URLs and input parameters to the underlying Git utility without adequate sanitization, an attacker can execute arbitrary system commands within the context of the host application.

Exploitation is constrained to scenarios where the host application processes untrusted repository references or user-supplied command arguments without prior sanitization.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Google Brotli decoder. An out-of-bounds write in the block-type switch handling in c/dec/decode.c can be triggered by a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. When an application decompresses untrusted Brotli data, this can lead to memory disclosure, denial of service, or potentially arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: brotli: Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This issue is rated Important. Exploitation requires that the target decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (for example HTTP content negotiated with Content-Encoding: br, or APIs such as Node.js zlib / fetch() that decode Brotli). The vulnerable path is reached with a malformed stream rather than typical well-formed encoder output. Red Hat Enterprise Linux compiler and runtime hardenings - including Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), Non-eXecutable (NX) memory, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux - increase the difficulty of turning this memory corruption into reliable code execution, though they do not eliminate crashes or all impact. Combined with the Attack Requirements noted by the CNA (CVSS v4 AT:P), Red Hat scores Attack Complexity as High and rates the flaw Important rather than Critical.

---

The Node.js packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux use either system version of brotli or bundled version. Some Node.js versions are marked "Not affected" because they utilize system brotli. For these versions, the Node.js package itself does not require updating. However, customers must still update the system brotli/libbrotli package to address the vulnerability for these Node.js installations.

Following is the overview of Node.js versions use system or bundled version.

- Node.js 22 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:22 module, uses system brotli.
- Node.js 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:24 modules, use bundled brotli.
- Node.js 22 and 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, provided via nodejs22 and nodejs24 use system brotli.

---

The .NET packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux may either use system version of brotli or bundled version. Following is the overview of .NET versions use system or bundled version.

- .NET 8.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet8.0 packages, use bundled brotli.
- .NET 9.0, 10.0, and 11.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet9.0, dotnet10.0, and dotnet11.0 use system brotli.

---

Red Hat OpenShift Service Mesh ships the vulnerable Brotli decoder code compiled into the istio-proxy; however, it is not affected by this security flaw by default. The vulnerable code is only reachable if a custom EnvoyFilter configures the envoy.filters.http.decompressor filter with Brotli - the Service Mesh control plane never generates this filter. All currently supported OpenShift Service Mesh streams (3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4) are not-affected and no fix is required. OpenShift Service Mesh 2.6 (out of support since 30 June 2026) and 3.0 (out of support since 31 October 2026) will not receive a fix for this CVE.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Image Composer (MIC) file. When an application attempts to count or extract frames from the malicious image, an improper state reset triggers an infinite loop. This non-advancing loop consumes excessive CPU resources and can hang application worker processes indefinitely.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via infinite loop during crafted MIC image parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can induce an infinite loop, exhausting worker CPU resources and resulting in a denial of service for applications handling untrusted image data. Within Red Hat environments, Pillow is deployed across numerous container images, machine learning frameworks, and automated backend services. Exploitation requires the optional olefile dependency to be present to register the Microsoft Image Composer format handler, and specifically targets workflows that query frame counts or process multi-frame images. Environments that do not inspect frame counts or do not have olefile installed are not vulnerable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. The PDF parser fails to limit recursion depth when reading nested PDF data structures such as arrays and dictionaries. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted, deeply nested PDF file to an application processing PDFs in append mode. This causes excessive recursion that crashes or terminates the worker process, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker could cause worker process termination and denial of service by submitting maliciously structured input files. However, exploitation is constrained to specific deployment workflows where an application utilizes Pillow to append image data onto preexisting, untrusted PDF documents. Systems and services that only process standard raster image formats or do not manipulate external PDF files in append mode are unaffected.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When saving compressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images into memory buffers rather than direct files, the library incorrectly calculates the required memory allocation. A remote attacker who supplies a crafted image for processing can trigger a heap-based buffer overflow, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) through process crashes. Additionally, uninitialized memory gaps can result in information disclosure by leaking remnants of previously stored data.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The attack complexity is high and also for services that do hit this code path (image upload → TIFF re-encode to BytesIO → return/upload), the minimal PoC reliably crashes the worker process. The heap corruption could plausibly be developed into RCE by a skilled attacker who has already compromised the same process enough to leak addresses, but that's a chained-exploit scenario, not a standalone wormable RCE.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted image with a width of zero to an application performing morphology operations. Because Pillow fails to validate zero-width image geometry during these operations, it attempts an out-of-bounds memory access before the buffer boundary, resulting in an application crash.

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds memory access on zero-width images
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important impact because remote, unauthenticated attackers can trigger an immediate denial of service by crashing target processes without requiring user intervention. In typical Red Hat product deployments, exposure is limited because triggering the flaw requires an application to actively process untrusted image input through morphological transformations. Workloads that parse standard image formats without performing morphology operations are not susceptible to this failure mode.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying a specially crafted FlashPix (FPX) image file to an application that processes untrusted inputs. Due to improper handling of image tile data during JPEG decoding, the library writes pixel data beyond the allocated memory buffer. This out-of-bounds write corrupts heap memory and can allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands or cause an application crash.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing a specially crafted Animated Portable Network Graphics (APNG) image. Pillow allocates memory for the full canvas dimensions before validating safety size limits during initial file opening. Processing such an image can exhaust available system memory and cause the application to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of service via crafted APNG image
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a denial of service through memory exhaustion without requiring user interaction or elevated privileges. Red Hat solutions such as OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform integrate Pillow to process arbitrary user or automated media uploads. Because full-canvas memory allocation occurs during initial file header ingestion prior to decompression safety limits being enforced, applications cannot rely on standard dimension safeguards to prevent worker termination.

Exposure is largely concentrated in containerized services and image-processing pipelines that handle untrusted animation uploads directly.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to achieve arbitrary code execution or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted lossless JPEG image to an application that downscales images or generates thumbnails. This issue occurs because the JPEG decoder fails to verify actual output dimensions against the allocated memory buffer during scaling, causing full-width image data to be written beyond buffer boundaries. Successful exploitation leads to heap memory corruption, resulting in an application crash or potential code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in ImagingJpegDecode
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The overflow only triggers when the application calls `draft()` or `thumbnail()` before loading the image. Direct `Image.open().load()` or `Image.open().resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Many image processing pipelines use `load()` followed by `resize()`, not `thumbnail()`. The libjpeg-turbo 3.x requirement, specific code path, and dimension threshold make this **not easily exploitable** across the entire Pillow install base.

Because parsing an invalid image file triggers an immediate segmentation fault within the native extension, the issue causes service disruption, although it does not compromise data confidentiality or allow arbitrary code execution.

Standard image parsing and reading pipelines that do not modify or append to existing PDF structures remain unaffected.

cwe.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Paint (MSP) image file to an application that processes image pixels. Due to missing expansion limits during decompression, the run-length encoding (RLE) decoder expands image data into an unbounded memory buffer, resulting in memory exhaustion and application crashes.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via unbounded memory expansion in MSP image decoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important impact because remote unauthenticated actors can induce an application denial of service by consuming all host or container memory, bypassing standard decompression safety limits. In Red Hat deployments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI and Red Hat Quay, service ingestion workflows accepting user-submitted graphics could suffer process termination or node instability when decoding untrusted assets. Deployments that process only verified internal content or do not expose image analysis to external inputs face substantially lower operational risk.

cwe.name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When rendering text using FreeType with an active stroke width, a failure during glyph loading can cause the library to free an uninitialized or stale memory pointer. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a malformed font to an application that renders stroked text. Successful exploitation can lead to memory corruption or an application crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via invalid pointer free during font rendering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker could cause memory corruption or terminate the application process without requiring privileges, leading to a denial of service. Across Red Hat product environments, Pillow operates as an underlying imaging component in automated services and containerized workloads. The vulnerability is only triggered if an application accepts untrusted font files from users and renders text using non-zero stroke widths, leaving services that utilize standard system fonts unaffected.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When converting multi-frame images into a multi-page PDF document, the library repeatedly scans previously assigned object identifiers, resulting in quadratic processing time. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a crafted image with a large frame count, causing excessive CPU consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via crafted multi-frame image conversion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause severe CPU exhaustion and service disruption by submitting minimal crafted inputs without needing system privileges. The elevated risk arises because even tiny files with declared high sequence numbers can tie up backend worker processes for prolonged periods in applications that convert user-provided graphics into multipage documents. Deployments remain unaffected if they only perform standard single-image rendering, validation, or do not expose multi-frame document export capabilities to untrusted users.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted PDF document to an application performing PDF append operations. Because the PDF parser fails to properly track cyclic or deeply nested object references, processing the malicious document can consume excessive CPU and memory resources or trigger an application crash.

Standard deployments that do not append to external PDF files or that generate new documents from trusted sources are unaffected.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Read

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When saving or re-encoding a Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) image containing inconsistent color map metadata, the encoder reads beyond an allocated memory buffer. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted image, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or information disclosure of heap memory.

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in TIFF encoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can supply crafted image files over network endpoints to cause process termination or heap memory disclosure without requiring privileges. The impact primarily concerns applications and containerized services that ingest untrusted image data and subsequently re-encode or save it using the libtiff-backed encoder while retaining metadata. Environments and workflows that only read, validate, or display images without writing them back out to TIFF format are not affected.

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This flaw can lead to information disclosure when handling compressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images. During incomplete decoding of image data, uninitialized buffer memory is not cleared before being converted into pixel rows. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted TIFF image to an application that decodes and returns or re-encodes the image, allowing them to view stale contents from heap memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Information disclosure via uninitialized buffer in TIFF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit default image parsing workflows to extract sensitive process memory without requiring privileges or triggering application crashes. In Red Hat environments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform, backend services that ingest user-provided images and return rendered thumbnails, previews, or re-encoded files inadvertently disclose previously freed heap data from concurrent or prior operations. The vulnerability requires processing compressed TIFF files where the decoder handles truncated image streams, meaning services that reject this format or never expose generated image outputs are not impacted.

cwe.name: External Control of File Name or Path

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying an untrusted submodule path. Because the library fails to properly validate destination paths before cloning repository data, an attacker can plant a malicious executable script into sensitive directories, such as the Git hooks folder. Subsequent Git operations then trigger the planted script, executing commands in the context of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: arbitrary code execution via improper submodule path validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because successful exploitation permits arbitrary code execution within the context of the underlying service or container. Although execution of arbitrary commands represents a critical consequence, the rating reflects the high complexity and prerequisites required, specifically that an application must accept user-controlled submodule paths and operate where default Git hook templates are absent. In Red Hat environments, such as Ansible Automation Platform, OpenShift AI, and Red Hat Satellite, impact is limited to workloads configured to process repository structures from untrusted or unauthenticated sources.
